topics.label: Lecture opening and cancer therapy learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students to the lecture and frames its subject and intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains local treatments that remove or damage tumors and the role of early detection in their success.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: mechanisms, benefits, and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how cytotoxic drugs damage cancer cells, their clinical benefits, and the toxicity and resistance that limit their use.

topics.label: Targeting hormone dependence in breast and prostate cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes blocking hormone signaling that particular breast and prostate cancers depend on for growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cell-cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how checkpoint-deficient cancer cells can be selectively targeted through irradiation or oncolytic adenoviruses.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking PARP can exploit defective BRCA-mediated DNA repair to kill cancer cells.

topics.label: Genome-guided targeting of oncogenic kinases
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics connect identifying oncogenic drivers with inhibiting activated kinases that sustain cancer growth.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitor selectivity, resistance, and clinical limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why kinase inhibitors can miss their targets or lose effectiveness as tumors adapt, and the resulting limits of treatment.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer treatments
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe using antibodies to target cancer-associated surface proteins and thereby block signaling or deliver cell-killing effects.

topics.label: T-cell recognition of tumors and checkpoint immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine evidence for immune recognition of tumors, how checkpoint blockade can restore T-cell activity, and the role of tumor neoantigens in response.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapies that bring or engineer T cells to recognize and attack tumor cells.

topics.label: Challenges in personalized cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic draws together treatment variability, resistance, and the need for biomarkers and genome sequencing to guide patient care.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends and the role of prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how changing cancer rates and outcomes relate to prevention and earlier diagnosis.

topics.label: Future cancer treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers future directions in cancer care and the ethical choices involved in treatment.

topics.label: Lecture closing reflection on childhood leukemia survival
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic ends the lecture with childhood leukemia survival as an example of treatment success and a reflection on the risks of changing approaches.
